note.summary: This chunk covers HMRC's power to assess and recover excessive repayments of tax (including interest) under s30 TMA 1970/Sch 18 FA98 para 52, the applicable time limits, and use of s29 TMA 1970 where overpayment arises from inflated expenses or tax paid. It also explains the limited circumstances in which a finalised assessment can be varied (s54, s49C, s49E/s49F, s50 TMA 1970), the practice of making alternative assessments where the correct tax head is uncertain, and guidance on requesting and reviewing a taxpayer's statement of assets and liabilities during an enquiry, including use of Schedule 36 information notices where a taxpayer refuses to provide one.

note.summary: This chunk covers HMRC's Enquiry Manual guidance on examining business records to challenge the credibility of a return, and on discovery assessments under Self Assessment. Enquiries are opened under s.9A (individuals), s.12AC (partnerships), Schedule 1A (claims) TMA 1970, or Schedule 18 FA 1998 (companies), and closed under specified corresponding provisions. Discovery assessments are used to recover tax loss when enquiry time limits have passed or no return was submitted, subject to conditions, and the Supreme Court in HMRC v Tooth confirmed discoveries cannot become 'stale' and there is no collective knowledge principle within HMRC. Discovery assessments require HO grade authorisation and are generally not used where an enquiry window is open or a return could still be issued/determined.

note.summary: This is HMRC's internal Enquiry Manual (EM), covering how HMRC conducts direct tax enquiries into Self Assessment returns. It addresses Human Rights Act considerations (right to fair trial and privacy) during enquiries, statutory record-keeping requirements, use of Schedule 36 FA 2008 information and inspection powers, and contract settlements (direct tax only, excluding VAT). Much of the manual's content is withheld under FOIA exemptions, and only a small fraction of the full manual (100 of ~561 sections) was mirrored in this run.

note.summary: This chunk covers multiple EM manual pages on the SA system outline: obligations to notify chargeability, return filing deadlines, record-keeping duties, and the structure of payments on account and balancing payments. It also covers interest, surcharges and penalties for late payment/filing, HMRC's enquiry powers under the 'process now/check later' regime, requirements that HMRC notices be in writing, staff confidentiality obligations under CRCA 2005, classification of settlements, and guidance on which year to open enquiries into when omissions may span multiple years.
